brief: A podcast player where episodes are constellations — listened ones glow, series form patterns

dominant_strengths: Strong metaphor: episodes as stars and series as constellations creates immediate poetic, memorable identity
Cohesive deep-space palette with teal/violet/amber accents reinforces the celestial theme without feeling kitschy
Legend panel cleanly encodes state (listened, unplayed, special) into a learnable visual language
dominant_weaknesses: Constellations float without hierarchy — no episode titles, dates, or grouping labels make navigation guesswork
Player card feels like a generic dark UI bolted onto a poetic canvas; visual languages don't reconcile
Spatial composition is loose: stars drift in dead space with no clear reading path or focal anchor
fix_priorities: Add hover/selected states with episode titles and series names so the metaphor becomes navigable, not decorative
Visually unify the player with the canvas (translucent, constellation-aware) instead of a flat card
Introduce subtle grouping (series labels, faint orbits) to give the starfield structural legibility
Tighten typography scale — the title and legend feel mismatched in weight and rhythm
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral and reflective soar on the constellation poetry, but behavioral usability lags badly without labels, hierarchy, or wayfinding.
rationale.intent_fit: It expresses the brief beautifully as a concept piece, but stops short of being a usable podcast player — the metaphor is rendered, not operationalized.
